features: Space Lens: A new view maps disk usage from any folder down to the whole disk as a treemap or sunburst. Scan any path or the full disk, drill into folders with breadcrumbs, and move what you no longer need to Trash right from the map. System locations are measured but protected, so tiles under /System, /Library and friends stay view-only.

Session Elevation: Privileged tasks (root scans, snapshot deletion, root thinning) ask for your administrator password once per session and nothing is installed; the old privileged helper, if present from a previous version, is removed automatically on first launch.
Live Scanning: Partial results appear while the scan runs, cancellable at any time, and the map rebalances after you move something to Trash without a full rescan.
One Scan, Two Charts: The scan runs once, only when you open Space Lens, and both the treemap and sunburst read the same tree; Settings > Interface picks which chart the page opens with.

Development Environments: A new catalog knows cache, log, session, package, VM disk and toolchain locations for 50+ tools including AI agents (Codex, Claude, opencode, jcode, Gemini), Docker Desktop, OrbStack, Rancher Desktop, Godot, JetBrains Toolbox, Qt, Sublime Text, Unity, VirtualBox and more. Locations that do not exist on your Mac never show up.

VM and Container Storage: The Development view lists real images, containers, volumes, build cache and VM disks from Docker, Colima, Lima, OrbStack, UTM, minikube and Docker Desktop, with sparse disk sizes and provisioned limits.
Stop Action: Running containers and VMs can be stopped right from the list without deleting anything; a rescan follows automatically.
Orphan Score Sorting: Leftover and Orphaned lists can sort by confidence score so the most certain wins come first.
Rule-Based Filters: Development paths are now tagged by kind (cache, logs, sessions, packages, VM disks, toolchains) and filtered through composable rules, ready for future filter toggles.
macOS Support: Minimum system raised to macOS 14.0 Sonoma; 26.x Tahoe and 27.x supported.
caveats: macOS 13 Ventura is no longer supported.

features: Privileged Helper Service (now retired): Version 4.4.0 introduced an installable privileged helper service for admin operations. The current version no longer installs anything; privileged tasks ask for your administrator password once per session and leave nothing behind.

App Lipo: There's a new Lipo(beta) view available in the menu which will show all universal apps and strip the app binary of the unused architectures to save some space. Universal apps will also show a Lipo button on the App Details view next to the Uninstall button to perform the same procedure on each app individually.
Multilingual Support: If you would like to help translate Pearcleaner to your language, please see GitHub issue #83
App List Size Sorting: You can now sort the sidebar app list alphabetically or by descending size. Click the User/System header to toggle or from the searchbar menu
Leftover Files: On first use, a warning/explanation sheet will be presented to the user
Finder Extension: When enabled, you can right click an app in finder and uninstall with Pearcleaner directly
Theme System: You can now select a base theme color for the application window
Folder Settings: Add more directories where Pearcleaner should search for app files
Progress: Show progress bar on startup when loading all app files with instant search enabled
App Icon: Show background color behind app icons in FilesView based on icon's average color mapping
Progress: Show time counter on regular file search views
Menubar Item: You can choose to access Pearcleaner from the menubar. This will show a slightly modified Mini Mode view.

Homebrew Cleanup: If you install apps using brew, you can now enable Homebrew cleanup in the settings to have Pearcleaner alert Homebrew that the app was removed externally from Homebrew and keep the brew app list synced.
Instant Search: Enable in settings to load app files on startup
Semantic Versioning: Going forward will use semver (Ex. v0.0.0)
Feature Alert: For each version, a feature alert will popup once on startup to show details
Leftover File Cleaning: Search your Mac for files leftover by uninstalled apps
Sidebar Drag Handle: Resize the sidebar in regular mode
Redesign UI/Settings/Icon: Some new buttons, layout changes, new official app icon and pear color theme accents
File Sort: Sort files alphabetically or by size
Socket File Removal: Finds socket files that aren't even visible in Finder with show hidden files enabled
OSLog Output: Will print errors to the Console app for easier troubleshooting
